== Biography ==
<blockquote>
Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McCullough celebrated their marriage in 1733. To them were born in due time, three sons, John, Robert, and Hugh.
</blockquote> <ref name="GlasgowHistory">[[Glasgow-590|William Melanchthon Glasgow]], ''History of the Glasgow Family'', [https://www.wikitree.com/photo/pdf/Glasgow-590 digital copy attached to Glasgow-590].</ref>
== Research Notes ==
* Similar to [[Glasgow-2990|John Glasgow (1740-)]]

=== 1831 Census ===

The '''1831 Irish Census''' for Lissane Parish, County Londonderry, lists two Glasgow households that may represent the next generation descended from [[Glasgow-548|Hugh Glasgow (abt. 1706–)]], patriarch of the Ulster Scots Glasgow family rooted in County Tyrone.

The two men listed — '''John Glasgow''' of Dromain and '''Robert Glasgow''' of Coltrim — were recorded in close proximity. Based on household sizes and composition, they may have been:
* '''Sons''' of [[Glasgow-549|John Glasgow (b. abt. 1735)]] or [[Glasgow-550|Robert Glasgow (b. abt. 1737)]], or  
* '''Grandsons''' of either man, continuing the family presence in Londonderry.

Robert’s household, with six males and five females, suggests he was a father of a large family, likely born c. 1780–1795. John’s all-male household (three males) may indicate a widower or older sons at home, suggesting a birth year c. 1770–1785.

While there is no definitive documentation, the proximity, naming patterns, and generational spacing support the theory that '''John and Robert Glasgow of the 1831 census were sons or grandsons of either John or Robert Glasgow, both sons of Hugh Glasgow (abt. 1706–)'''.

<ref>[http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1831/Londonderry/Lissane/ 1831 Irish Census – National Archives of Ireland]</ref>

=== Corrected assessment ===

John is chronologically a possible, but unproved, direct father of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3927|John Glasgow]] of Inishrush.  No located record distinguishes him from the traditional brother [[Glasgow-550|Robert Glasgow]].  The naming pattern in the younger documented family and the separate 1740 Hugh Glasgow household are research clues, not proof of a parent-child link.

== Research Notes ==
A possible identification concerns John Glasco, charged at Bow Street. John Glasco, Esq., said he was an officer on the Staff and was brought before the Bow Street magistrate charged with wounding patrolman John Smith. The reported incident occurred on Tuesday night after the play in Covent Garden; Glasco was committed.<ref>The Times, 2 May 1799, p.3, Public Office, Bow Street; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/32820363/ record].</ref> Allegation and committal are not conviction. Military status is self-reported and unconfirmed; no Irish origin or kin is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glascow, London chairman. John Glascow, a chairman, said he saw a man in black running with pistols after Martha Ray was shot in Covent Garden.<ref>Derby Mercury, provider-labelled 19 March 1779, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394231375/ record]; Old Bailey original, printed p.207; [https://www.dhi.ac.uk/san/ob/1770s/177904040005.gif record]; Old Bailey Proceedings, James Hackman record t17790404-3; event dating only; [https://www.oldbaileyonline.org/record/t17790404-3 record].</ref> The Old Bailey indictment specifies that Martha Ray was shot on 7 April 1779 (printed p.207); that is the event date, not the indictment or newspaper publication date. The newspaper describes evidence after the shooting, not established trial testimony. Its March provider label is incorrect. The identification remains uncertain.
